creep_data.CD_dt: [Day] Time difference: for drying creep t-t0 (since exposure), for basic or total creep t-t' (since mechanical loading)

creep_test.CT_Jshift: [uE/MPa] Compliance function shift due to CT_timeShift, see  M. Rasoolinejad, S. Rahimi-Aghdam, Z.P.Bažant: Statistical filtering of useful concrete creep data from imperfect laboratory tests, Materials and structures, 2018
creep_test.CT_RH_test: [%] Environmental humidity H in % during the test (99 means a sealed specimen, 100 means storage in water, 101 steam, 85 moist) denoted often as H0 .
creep_test.CT_creepType: ['total','basic','drying','total?','basic?','drying?'] Creep type recorded in dataset. Total is understood as basic+drying creep
creep_test.CT_creepType_CTU: Only for sorting data at CTU in Prague. ERROR means wrong data for some reason.
creep_test.CT_dataTimeScale: [ENUM] Timescale in literature figure or data source
creep_test.CT_elastic_strain: TRUE if elastic strain was measured in the beginning of creep test
creep_test.CT_f_cmCyl_t0: [MPa] Cylinder compressive strength of concrete at time on loading.
creep_test.CT_heating: [ENUM] Type of heating to higher temperature, either before the test or during the test
creep_test.CT_original_database_ID: [e.g. 1] Source of data if taken from another database
creep_test.CT_original_database_text_id: [e.g. c_001_01] Data reference text from original database
creep_test.CT_sigma: [MPa] Sustained stress during the test. Plus means compression.
creep_test.CT_sigmaTof_cmCyl_t0: [-] Stress level = stress / (compressive strength at the beginning of loading).
creep_test.CT_tPrime: [day] Age at loading, or age t0 at the beginning of environmental exposure.
creep_test.CT_temperature: [°C] Temperature maintained during the creep test.
creep_test.CT_timeShift: [days] Time shift due to experimental error, see  M. Rasoolinejad, S. Rahimi-Aghdam, Z.P.Bažant: Statistical filtering of useful concrete creep data from imperfect laboratory tests, Materials and structures, 2018

literature.L_authorYear: [e.g. Acker:1998] Unique reference in the form author:year
literature.L_authors: [e.g. Bažant, Z.P. and Baweja, S.] Authors
literature.L_oldOrig: [TEXT] Reference from old database, kept for backtracking and potentially could be removed
literature.L_oldRefNum: [INT] Reference from old database, kept for backtracking and potentially could be removed
literature.L_oldRefText: [TEXT] Reference from old database, kept for backtracking and potentially could be removed

mix.M_ElasticMod28: [MPa] Modulus of elasticity at 28 days of age in MPa.
mix.M_aToBinder: [- Auto] Aggretate to binder ratio. All admixtures are calulated with cement, i.e. aggregates/(cement+slag+silica fume+ ...)
mix.M_aToc: [- Auto] The aggregate-cement ratio by weight. Automatically calculated by a trigger.
mix.M_accelerator: [kg/m3] Accelerator content. If it was in liters, it was recalculated to kg with density of 1.1 kg/l.
mix.M_agg_all_mass: [kg/m3 Auto] Mass of coarse aggregates. Automatically calculated by a trigger as the sum of fine and coarse aggregates..
mix.M_agg_coarse_mass: [kg/m3] Mass of coarse aggregates (size above 4-5 mm depending on country and standard)
mix.M_agg_fine_mass: [kg/m3] Mass of fine aggregates (size up to 4-5 mm depending on country and standard)
mix.M_airEntrAgent: [kg/m3] Air entraining agent's content. If it was in liters, it was recalculated to kg with density of 1.1 kg/l.
mix.M_cem_ASTM_type: [Type I, Type II, ...] cement type according to ASTM C150
mix.M_cem_EN_strength_class: [MPa]. Cement strength class, compressive strength at 28 days on 1:3 mortars, according to EN 197-1
mix.M_cem_EN_type: ['CEM I', 'CEM II', ...] Cement type according to EN 197-1
mix.M_cem_EN_type_sub: ['A-S', 'B-S', ...] Subtype of cement, such as CEM II/A-S, according to EN 197-1
mix.M_cem_ModelCode_type: ['SL Slow hardening','N Normal','R Rapid hardening','RS rapid hardening high strength'] Cement type according to CEB Model Code 1990.
mix.M_cem_mass: [kg/m3] Cement content without mineral admixtures, in kg/m3. Put Portland part of blended cement here, if you know exactly the amount of admixtures and mention the admixtures in particular columns. If you do not know the substitution exactly, put here the whole blend (e.g. CEM II/B-S has 21-35% of slag).
mix.M_country: [ENUM such as 'CA'] Country, ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 Country Codes In Mysql Enum Format
mix.M_expansiveAdmixture: [kg/m3] Expansive admixture's content. If it was in liters, it was recalculated to kg with density of 1.1 kg/l.
mix.M_fcmCube28d: [MPa] Mean compressive strength of concrete cube at 28 days of age in MPa.
mix.M_fcmCyl28d: [MPa] Mean compressive strength of concrete cylinders at 28 days of age in MPa.
mix.M_limestone: [kg/m3] Ground limestone content as a filler.
mix.M_original_database_name: [TEXT] Name of source database, if any
mix.M_otherFiller_description: [ENUM] Other fillers such as Calcined clay
mix.M_retarder: [kg/m3] Retarder content. If it was in liters, it was recalculated to kg with density of 1.1 kg/l.
mix.M_shrinkageRedAdmixture: [kg/m3] Shrinkage reducing admixture's content. If it was in liters, it was recalculated to kg with density of 1.1 kg/l.
mix.M_superplast: [kg/m3] Superplasticizer content. If it was in liters, it was recalculated to kg with density of 1.1 kg/l.  NULL=we do not know, 0=no superplasticizer.
mix.M_viscousModAg: [kg/m3] Viscous modifying agent controlling fresh concrete properties, content.
mix.M_wToBinder: [- Auto] Water to binder ratio. All admixtures are calulated with cement, i.e. water/(cement+slag+silica fume+ ...)
mix.M_wToc: [- Auto] The water-cement ratio by weight. Cement=blended cement if it is made by a producer as a bag. Additives (slag, fly ash, silica) added externally go to another fields. Automatically calculated by a trigger.
mix.M_waterReducer: [kg/m3] Water reducer content. If it was in liters, it was recalculated to kg with density of 1.1 kg/l.
mix.M_water_mass: [kg/m3] Water mass in kg/m3. Water content should be effective, i.e. added water - full absorption capacity of aggregates. Several articles reported added water over dried aggregates which is in the database.

shrinkage_data.SD_dt: [Day] Time difference t-t0 (for drying and total shrinkage). For autogenous shrinkage, SD_dt=t-ST_t_dryingFrom
shrinkage_data.SD_strain: [uE] Shrinkage strain. Minus is contraction, plus expansion. Zero for autogeneous shrinkage should be at the final setting time (see J.R.T. Filho et al., Materials 2019).

shrinkage_test.ST_RH_test: [%] Environmental humidity H in % during the test (99 means a sealed specimen, 100 means storage in water, denoted often as H0
shrinkage_test.ST_dataTimeScale: [ENUM] Timescale in literature figure or data source. Critical for early-age behavior - linear scale does not capture short times.
shrinkage_test.ST_f_cmCyl_tDryingFrom: [MPa] Cylinder compressive strength of concrete at the beginning of drying
shrinkage_test.ST_heating: [ENUM] Type of heating to higher temperature, either before the test or during the test
shrinkage_test.ST_original_database_ID: [e.g. 1] Source of data if taken from another database
shrinkage_test.ST_original_database_text_id: [e.g. c_001_01] Data reference text from original database
shrinkage_test.ST_shrinkageType: ['autogenous','drying shrinkage','total','autogenous?','drying shrinkage?','total?'] Type of shrinkage of a specimen. Total is combination of autogenous and drying, not differentiated.
shrinkage_test.ST_shrinkageType_CTU: Only for sorting data at CTU in Prague. ERROR means wrong data for some reason.
shrinkage_test.ST_t_dryingFrom: [day] Time for zero strain for autogenous shrinkage. Or beginning of external drying.
shrinkage_test.ST_tmpShape: No idea what that means (only 'init' in the DB)- to be eliminated?

specimen.S_H0: [%] Environmental humidity of specimen preconditioning (usually after water storage and prior to a test), if unsealed. 99 means a sealed specimen, 100 means storage in water/wet, 101 steam, 85 moist.
specimen.S_T_curing: [°C] Curing temperature of specimen before testing
specimen.S_VToS: [mm] Volume to surface ratio. Depends on drying surface.
specimen.S_geometry: [ENUM] Geometry description. Consequece for drying kinetics -  Cylinder dries from circumference, Prism from 4 sides, Slab from top/bottom or both, Cube from 6 sides
specimen.S_height: [mm] Height of specimen. Applies to ALL shapes
specimen.S_length: [mm] Length of Prism's cross-section edge (smaller), or Slab's length (smaller)
specimen.S_width: [mm] Width of rectangular Prism, or rectangular Slab (i.e. different from S_length)
